I have farmed this wheat-maize land for many years, so I will start from what has worked and only adjust a little. I have 18 mu, and only 2 people at home, with some off-farm work, so I do not want a plan that needs too much hand labor. I will keep the full 18 mu in the wheat-maize rotation. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, not old saved seed, because the stand is more even and the yield is steadier with irrigation. I will keep fertilizer on the safe side, because losing yield hurts more than spending a bit more on fertilizer. Wheat needs a little more feeding in my place, especially nitrogen, and I will still give phosphorus under the base fertilizer because our land responds to it. Potassium I will not push too high, but I will not skip it either. Wheat will get about 3 irrigations in a normal year: one after sowing if moisture is short, one at jointing, and one at grain filling if needed. For maize, I will use hybrid seed. Around here, if the wheat comes off on time and the summer rain is decent, maize can still yield well, but I will not cut fertilizer too much. I will use no-tillage or very light direct seeding after wheat to save labor and grab time, then rely on 2 irrigations if rainfall is not enough. On pesticide, I will not spray blindly, but I will plan for 2 times on each crop, because weeds and insects can take yield fast if I wait too long.
